outcome: level of satisfaction with the outcome of the perineal repair
cohort: The study included 5,328 primiparous women in Sweden who sustained either a spontaneous second-degree tear (n=4,323) or an episiotomy (n=1,005) between 2014 and 2019.
finding: Approximately one-third of women with either a spontaneous tear or an episiotomy reported mild or moderate dyspareunia at one year, while episiotomy was associated with a higher adjusted odds ratio for strong or unbearable dyspareunia and dissatisfaction with the outcome.
